name: canli-backtest-mcp

tools.name: list_factors
tools.description: The point-in-time factors pit_factor builds from SEC filings, and what each measures.

tools.name: pit_factor
tools.description: Build a factor from SEC filings for a list of tickers, monthly from start to end, using only what had been filed by each date (restatements invisible until filed). Writes a signal CSV for backtest_signal. Values are what companies reported to the SEC in XBRL, as filed by each date; a company that files late, files outside XBRL or changes its tags can be missing.

factor.description: One of roa, gross_margin, operating_margin, revenue_growth, asset_growth, accruals, or level:<measure> (revenue, net_income, assets, ...).

tickers.description: Tickers (or CIKs) to compute it for.

out_file.description: Where to write the signal CSV; default a new temporary file.

tools.name: backtest_signal
tools.description: Backtest a signal against your prices: rank, long and short quantiles, rebalance, trading only on what was known lag_days earlier, costs on actual trades. Every reply holds the result against the crises its dates cover and lists the ones it does not. With capital_usd and dollar_volume_file, orders fill only as far as the market traded, pay square-root impact, and the reply shows the Sharpe at each size the market can take. Pass ledger to judge the best of a search against all of it. A backtest measures one path of history under these costs; it does not establish that the signal will keep working.

prices_file.description: CSV: a date column (YYYY-MM-DD) and one column of closing prices per ticker.

signal_file.description: CSV in the same shape; each row dated when its values became known (pit_factor writes this).

rebalance.description: Default monthly; or every N trading days.

lag_days.description: Trading days between a signal becoming known and trading on it. Default 1, the minimum.

side.description: Default long_short: long the top quantile, short the bottom.

quantile.description: Fraction of ranked names in each leg. Default 0.2.

cost_bps.description: Cost per unit traded, in basis points. Default 10.

min_names.description: Skip a rebalance with fewer ranked names. Default 5.

capital_usd.description: Size to trade at, in dollars. Needs dollar_volume_file. Orders fill only up to max_participation of recent volume and pay square-root impact, and the reply adds a capacity curve.

dollar_volume_file.description: CSV like prices_file with daily dollar volume. price_panel writes one from adjusted closes, which understates older volume by the dividends paid since.

max_participation.description: Largest share of a name's average daily dollar volume one order can take. Default 0.1.

impact_coefficient.description: Y in impact = Y x daily volatility x sqrt(participation). Default 1.

crisis_drawdown_limit.description: A drawdown beyond this inside one crisis counts as a rupture. Default 0.5.

ledger.description: Record this run in a search ledger (created if new) and judge it against every run recorded there.

label.description: The variant's name in the ledger. Default: the settings.

tools.name: proof_filings
tools.description: Add what companies filed to a signed, append-only ledger: each figure with its filing, and a restatement line whenever a later filing changes one. Re-running adds only what is new. It shows the lines were not altered afterwards, not that a figure is right.

ledger_file.description: The ledger file; started if new.

key_file.description: Signing key (PEM); created if new. Default ~/.canli/proof-key.pem.

annotations.title: Add company filings to a proof ledger

tools.name: proof_file
tools.description: Record a file's hash in a signed, append-only ledger, a backtest result or a returns file, so anyone can later check this exact file existed by then. Nothing else about the file is claimed.

ledger_file.description: The ledger file; started if new.

file.description: The file to record: a backtest's result, a returns file, a league entry. Only its hash goes in the ledger.

annotations.title: Record a file in a proof ledger

tools.name: proof_verify
tools.description: Check a proof ledger from the file alone: every hash, order and signature, and any heads published elsewhere. Says which line first fails.

anchors.description: Heads published elsewhere: each must still be in the file.

tools.name: proof_find
tools.description: Look up a file, company or concept in a proof ledger. No record means only that this ledger holds none, not that anything is wrong.

file.description: Or the file itself, hashed here.

company.description: Company name or CIK as recorded.

tools.name: league_new
tools.description: Start a paper league: a schedule of rounds and rules with a hash to publish. No prizes, no stakes and nobody's money.

league_dir.description: A folder for the league's rules, ledger and entries.

first_close.description: When entries for the first round close; scoring starts the next trading day.

days_per_round.description: Calendar days from one close to the next, and each round's scoring span. Default 7.

min_names.description: Fewest scored names an entry needs. Default 20.

tools.name: league_commit
tools.description: Commit a league entry before its round closes: only the hash of its CSV of ticker,score goes in the ledger, and the file is shown after the round. Only the latest commit counts, so revealing whichever of several did best is refused.

file.description: The entry: a CSV of ticker,score, higher meaning expected to do better. Only its hash is recorded now.

entrant_key_file.description: The entrant's own signing key (PEM), created if new. A name belongs to the key that first committed under it, so nobody else can replace an entrant's entry.

key_file.description: The league's signing key for its ledger (PEM); created if new.

tools.name: league_score
tools.description: Score a paper league from its files and prices, repeatable by anyone: each entrant's rank correlation with what followed, set against the best luck gives across that many entrants, how different each is from the rest, and a paper book of the top entrants chosen on earlier rounds only.

prices_file.description: CSV: a date column and one column of closing prices per ticker. Everyone re-running the table needs the same file.

book_size.description: How many top entrants the paper book combines. Default 5.

tools.name: exchange_new
tools.description: Start a paper exchange where different AI agents and scripted traders (market makers, momentum, value, deleveragers, stop-losses, levered longs) trade in limit order books, with margin rules and forced selling, plus shocks at set steps. Made-up assets and money, reproducible from a seed.

exchange_file.description: The exchange's state file; must not exist yet.

seed.description: The same seed and the same orders give the same market. Default 1.

personas.description: How many scripted traders of each kind. Default 8 market makers, 8 value, 6 momentum, 8 noise, 4 deleveragers, 4 stop-loss, 4 levered longs.

starting_cash.description: Made-up money each agent starts with. Default 100000.

maintenance_margin.description: An agent whose equity falls below this share of its gross positions is sold out by force. Default 0.25.

leverage.description: How many times its equity an agent may hold in positions when it opens them. Default 2.

shocks.description: Things that happen at set steps. Agents see them only through prices.

kind.description: value: the asset's true worth jumps. liquidity: market makers pull their quotes for some steps. block_sale: one large holder sells at market.

percent.description: For value: how far it jumps.

tools.name: exchange_join
tools.description: Join a paper exchange as an agent. Returns the token its other calls need, so no agent can act as another.

about.description: What this agent is, such as its model and its brief. Shown in the report.

tools.name: exchange_view
tools.description: What an agent in a paper exchange can see: the books, recent trades and its own account. No other agent's positions.

token.description: The token exchange_join gave this agent, so no agent can act as another.

depth.description: Price levels to show on each side; default 5.

tools.name: exchange_orders
tools.description: Send an agent's limit orders, market orders and cancels for the coming step of a paper exchange. An empty list passes.

token.description: The token exchange_join gave this agent, so no agent can act as another.

order_id.description: Without it, all your resting orders go.

orders.description: What to do in the coming step. An empty list says you are passing, so the step can close.

annotations.title: Send orders to a paper exchange

tools.name: exchange_step
tools.description: Move a paper exchange on. Waits for every joined agent to act, so nobody moves time on the others.

force.description: Close the step even though a joined agent has not acted.

tools.name: exchange_report
tools.description: What happened in a paper exchange: each asset's worst fall and recovery, spreads and depth, who gained and lost, forced selling and the longest chain of it, and a hash anyone can check by replaying.

tools.name: exchange_run
tools.description: Run a whole paper exchange of scripted traders in one call and report it: for comparing set-ups, such as how much leverage turns a shock into a cascade. A simulation, not a forecast.

seed.description: The same seed and the same orders give the same market. Default 1.

personas.description: How many scripted traders of each kind. Default 8 market makers, 8 value, 6 momentum, 8 noise, 4 deleveragers, 4 stop-loss, 4 levered longs.

starting_cash.description: Made-up money each agent starts with. Default 100000.

maintenance_margin.description: An agent whose equity falls below this share of its gross positions is sold out by force. Default 0.25.

leverage.description: How many times its equity an agent may hold in positions when it opens them. Default 2.

shocks.description: Things that happen at set steps. Agents see them only through prices.

kind.description: value: the asset's true worth jumps. liquidity: market makers pull their quotes for some steps. block_sale: one large holder sells at market.

percent.description: For value: how far it jumps.

tools.name: agent_consensus
tools.description: Combine several AI agents' probabilities, and count how many independent views they really hold, from how their errors move together: five models that share their mistakes are not five votes. Weights each by its record on settled questions.

agents.description: Each agent's probability for each question.

outcomes.description: Questions already settled. Their forecasts give each agent a record; the rest are combined.

annotations.title: Combine agents' forecasts and count independent views

tools.name: find_diversifiers
tools.description: Rank candidate strategies by what they add to a book: independent bets added first, then how they behave on the book's worst days, with return shown last and never used to rank. Correlation first.

book_file.description: A CSV of the book's daily returns: date, then one column per strategy or one for the whole book.

candidates_file.description: A CSV of candidates' daily returns: date, then one column each.

min_days.description: Days a candidate must share with the book; default 252.

tools.name: arena_new
tools.description: Start a paper market for AI agents to trade in: made-up assets and made-up money, with scripted traders, reproducible from a seed. Nothing here represents or reaches a real security, token or currency.

arena_file.description: The arena's state file; must not exist yet.

seed.description: The same seed and the same orders give the same market. Default 1.

starting_cash.description: Made-up money each agent starts with. Default 100000.

bots.description: Scripted traders that keep the market moving: noise, value and momentum in turn. Default 6.

tools.name: arena_orders
tools.description: Send paper orders for an agent in an arena, for the coming auction. No short selling and no borrowing.

orders.description: Replaces this agent's orders for the coming step. No short selling and no borrowing.

annotations.title: Send paper orders to an arena

tools.name: arena_step
tools.description: Clear a paper arena's next call auctions at one price per asset, and show prices and standings. Paper only.

tools.name: crisis_replay
tools.description: Hold any strategy's daily returns against named market crises (2000-02 dot-com bust, 2008-09 bank crisis, 2011 US downgrade and euro debt scare, 2013 taper tantrum in bonds and others): its return, drawdown and worst day in each one its dates fully cover, and the crises it was not there for, listed as untested and never as passed.

returns_file.description: CSV: a date column (YYYY-MM-DD) and one column of daily returns per strategy, at most 50.

drawdown_limit.description: A drawdown beyond this inside one crisis counts as a rupture. Default 0.5.

tools.name: cpcv
tools.description: Combinatorial purged cross-validation of a search: choose the best trial on training days, score it on held-out blocks, with purge and embargo at the edges, for every choice of blocks, stitched into whole paths. Returns the spread of out-of-sample Sharpes against the in-sample one. Splits can run as shards on other machines and merge back. Paths share days and data, so their spread is not a confidence interval and they are not independent tests.

returns_file.description: CSV: a date column and one column of daily returns per trial (breadth_book's out_file, say). At least two trials.

groups.description: Blocks history is cut into. Default 10.

test_groups.description: Blocks in each test set. Default 2.

purge_days.description: Training days dropped before each test block: at least the horizon the trials' returns look ahead over. Default 5.

embargo_days.description: Training days dropped after each test block. Default 5.

shard.description: Run only splits s with s mod of = index, to spread the work over machines.

out_file.description: Write the shard as JSON here.

merge_files.description: Instead of running: shard files to merge into one result.

tools.name: price_panel
tools.description: Build a price panel from free sources for breadth_book or backtest_signal: the tickers you name or an index fund's current holdings, daily adjusted closes and dollar volume, and each company's Fama-French industry from its SEC SIC code, written as CSV files.

index_fund.description: Or an index fund or ETF whose current holdings make the universe: IVV (S&P 500), IJH (mid caps), IJR (small caps), QQQ, VTI...

max_names.description: With index_fund: the largest holdings to take. Default 500.

out_dir.description: Folder for prices.csv, dollar_volume.csv and groups.csv. Default: a new temporary folder.

tools.name: breadth_signals
tools.description: The cross-sectional signals breadth_book builds sleeves from: momentum, reversal, low volatility and beta, idiosyncratic risk, lottery demand, skewness, price delay, seasonality and liquidity, each with its formula's source and the data it needs.

tools.name: breadth_book
tools.description: Build many weakly correlated sleeves (every signal inside every group of names) from your price panel and trade them as one netted account, ALPHAC's breadth lab: rank-weighted within each group, overlapping portfolios, hedged and scaled to a volatility target, costs on actual trades. Returns the book netted and standalone, the netting ratio, effective independent bets and ideas, and writes every sleeve's returns as a training dataset. A sleeve built on many signals and groups is a search: report the number of sleeves, keep a period untouched for the test, and judge the book there, not on the years used to choose it.

prices_file.description: CSV: a date column and one column of closing (total-return) prices per ticker.

groups_file.description: CSV with columns ticker,group (an industry, say): one sleeve per signal per group. Default: one group, the whole panel.

dollar_volume_file.description: CSV like prices_file with daily dollar volume: adds the liquidity signals, a $5m liquidity floor and cost tiers by volume.

signals.description: Signals from breadth_signals. Default: every one the data allows.

min_names.description: Fewest eligible names a group needs at a rebalance. Default 10.

smoothing.description: Rebalances whose weights are averaged (overlapping portfolios). Default 3 (monthly), 4 (weekly).

cost_bps.description: Cost per unit traded when no dollar volume is given. Default 10.

split_date.description: Report the book before and after this date: choose on the first part, judge on the second.

out_file.description: Where to write every sleeve's daily returns (CSV, one column per sleeve): a dataset to train or select on. Its specs go beside it as .specs.json. Default: a new temporary file.

ledger.description: Record the netted book in a search ledger and judge it against every run there.

tools.name: breadth_sweep
tools.description: Run a grid of breadth-book settings (signal sets, smoothing, target volatility, costs, minimum names) in parallel on every core of this machine, or as shards other machines run and merge_files joins. Every combination counts as a trial: the best Sharpe is set against what the best of that many trials reaches by luck, and with split_date the chosen settings are scored after the split.

prices_file.description: CSV of prices: date column, one column per ticker (price_panel writes one).

dollar_volume_file.description: Optional dollar volume CSV with the same dates.

grid.description: Values to try for each setting; every combination runs (at most 400).

split_date.description: Choose on dates up to this one; report the chosen settings after it.

workers.description: Threads; default one less than this machine's cores.

shard.description: Run only combinations k with k mod of = index, to spread a sweep over machines.

out_file.description: Write the results (or the shard) as JSON here.

merge_files.description: Instead of running: shard files to merge into one result.

tools.name: effective_bets
tools.description: How many independent bets a set of return series holds: the participation ratio of their weekly correlations (n for unrelated series, 1 for copies), and with families, the families' bets and the ideas they cluster into.

returns_file.description: CSV: a date column and one column of daily returns per series (breadth_book's out_file, say).

family_separator.description: Columns named family<sep>member are grouped into families, e.g. "@" for breadth_book's signal@group. Default: no families.

threshold.description: Families whose books correlate at least this much (in absolute value, average linkage) count as one idea. Default 0.5.

tools.name: annotation_packet
tools.description: Start a labelled dataset: figures (company, measure, period, value) are checked by machine against the SEC filings and written as blind CSV packets for two or more people to label, with guidelines and a key holding the machine labels.

task.description: A name for the task, e.g. q3-revenue-check: the folder the files go in.

items.description: Figures to label: company, measure, period, value (and unit), as for verify_claims.

items_file.description: Or a JSONL file of the same objects, up to 2,000.

text.description: Or a draft about one company (an AI's answer, say): every figure in it with a measure and a period becomes an item. Needs company.

company.description: With text: the company the draft is about.

annotators.description: Packets to write, one per person. Default 2: two people label every item independently.

assisted.description: Show the machine's label and the filed figure in the packets. Default false (blind), so agreement with the machine means something.

out_dir.description: Folder for the task folder. Default: a new temporary folder.

tools.name: annotation_agreement
tools.description: Read filled annotation packets: how often the people agree (Cohen's kappa), how often they agree with the machine, and every disagreement.

task_dir.description: The folder annotation_packet wrote, with the filled packets in it.

tools.name: annotation_gold
tools.description: Merge filled annotation packets and a reviewer's decisions into a gold dataset (JSONL: each item's label, who decided it, the machine label and source) with a datasheet of agreement and hashes.

task_dir.description: The folder annotation_packet wrote, with the filled packets in it.

reviews.description: A reviewer's decisions on items the annotators disagreed on.

instructions: Backtests that refuse lookahead. Build a point-in-time factor from SEC filings with pit_factor (or bring your own signal CSV, each row dated when it was known), then run backtest_signal against your own prices CSV. Pass the same ledger name to every backtest_signal call in one search: the reply judges the best variant against all of them. For breadth, price_panel builds a free price panel (an index fund's holdings, prices, dollar volume and industries), breadth_book builds a sleeve for every signal in every industry from one price panel and trades them as one netted account; effective_bets counts the independent bets in any set of return series. For a search, cpcv scores the chosen variant on held-out blocks across many paths, and crisis_replay holds any returns against named crises. proof_filings and proof_file keep a signed, append-only record; league_new, league_commit and league_score run a paper league scored after the fact; arena_new, arena_orders and arena_step are a paper market for agents, with made-up assets and money. For datasets, annotation_packet, annotation_agreement and annotation_gold turn figures into a gold set people have checked against the filings.
